PullRequest.Title: HTML: resolve relative links only against hierarchical base URIs
PullRequest.Body:
The HTML server's `resolveReference` resolved relative hrefs against any `<base href>`. With a non-hierarchical base, a relative href took over the base's scheme and query, producing document links whose scheme the language service would otherwise filter out.

Relative references are now only resolved against `http`, `https`, `file` or the document's own scheme. Any other base yields no link, which `DocumentContext.resolveReference` allows (`string | undefined`).

## How to test
- `cd extensions/html-language-features/server && pnpm run test` → 72 passing, including the new `Only resolves relative references against hierarchical bases`.
- Manually in Code OSS:
  - With `<base href="command:...">`, a relative href is no longer a link.
  - A relative link without `<base>` still opens the target file.
  - An `https:` `<base>` still resolves, e.g. `https://example.com/docs/guide/page.html?q=1`.
- ESLint on the changed files passes.

Scenarios.Scenario: HTML document-link discovery for an open or changed document
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing LSP documentLink request enters htmlServer, enumerates embedded language modes serially, and the HTML language service scans link-bearing attributes; each relative reference synchronously calls the changed resolver before the response can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing LSP documentLink request and response between the editor and HTML language server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per document-link refresh; all link candidates are processed locally inside that request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request crossed the same IPC boundary and scanned/resolved document links before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The local scan and reference resolution must finish before the response, but the diff adds no IPC round trips.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of relative link attributes in the document after the language service's own candidate filtering. For normal file/http/https bases, each candidate adds only a Set membership check because the OR short-circuits before parsing documentUri. For a disallowed non-hierarchical base, the document URI is parsed per candidate but the old dirname/resolvePath/stringification work is skipped.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Language modes are awaited serially in htmlServer; URI parsing and path resolution are synchronous, with no introduced worker, queue, fan-out, or parallel boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The DocumentContext is recreated per request and has no reference-result cache. Warm HTML model state does not change the resolver cost. No cache is defeated; the newly rejected base case avoids downstream resolution rather than retaining negative entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the per-reference synchronous call path and short-circuit behavior from the changed resolver and htmlServer call site; exact language-service scan internals are dependency-owned but do not alter the before/after conclusion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Documents can contain many links, but common hierarchical bases avoid the only repeated documentUri parse. Non-hierarchical bases are uncommon and now perform less total resolution work, so there is no evidenced user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed guard is constant-time on common bases and reduces work for rejected bases; the uncommon same-scheme non-hierarchical case adds a small parse without evidence of material latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: HTML or embedded-CSS completion while editing a relative URL
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing LSP completion request obtains settings, creates a DocumentContext, and synchronously invokes HTML doComplete2 or CSS doComplete2; any reference resolution used to produce completion paths is on the response critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing LSP completion request and response between the editor and HTML language server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per completion trigger; one language mode handles the cursor position.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same completion request and response boundary existed; only a local scheme eligibility check is new.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion computation must finish before suggestions are returned, but the diff adds no IPC, filesystem, or network operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Completion is scoped to the active cursor and its relevant URL context rather than every document link. Standard file/http/https bases short-circuit after one Set lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One completion mode is selected per cursor position and awaited for the request. Reference resolution is synchronous and introduces no concurrent I/O or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: HTML parse state is held in the existing language-model cache; the new scheme Set is module-scoped. The DocumentContext is per request, and the change neither invalidates model caches nor adds retained cache keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from htmlServer mode selection and htmlMode/cssMode call sites that the changed resolver is local, synchronous work on an existing completion path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Dependency internals determine whether a completion request invokes the resolver once or a small bounded number of times, but there is no changed boundary call or collection-wide work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded local checking and no expensive boundary, retained state, or concurrency amplification.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across the full two-file diff. Traced document-link and completion critical paths, repeated URI work, caches, concurrency, and IPC boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not establish a shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame attribution.
